result:
Happy to work through this with you. I read the spreadsheet description you pasted. It's simple: one row per loan, with seed, packets, borrower, date out and date back. About a third of the "Date back" cells are empty. That gap is probably where the real problem is, so I'd like to understand it before thinking about what to build.

Seed libraries don't work like book libraries. Often people don't return the same packets. They return seed they saved from their own harvest, months later, in different amounts, or sometimes nothing at all. So a blank "Date back" might mean the seeds are still out. It might mean the person never intended to return any. It might also mean the seeds came back and nobody wrote it down. Each of those calls for something different. The first two are about following up with people, and the last is about making it easier to record returns.

When you look at those empty cells, what do they usually mean, and what goes wrong for the garden because of them?
